item.title: [Sports Gazette] Max Muncy: The Dodgers Unsung Hero - Sports Gazette
item.dc:creator: Conner Rowntree

item.content:encoded:
Muncy, the longest-tenured Dodger, joined the organization in 2017 on a minor league deal after being cut from the then-Oakland Athletics. The hard-hitting third baseman was called up to the Dodgers in 2018, and in less than a decade, Muncy went from nearly being out of baseball to cementing his legacy as an all-time great.
“I remember a guy that just got DFA’d that was sort of kicked to the curb by an organization that didn’t believe in him,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said of Muncy. “He was close to being out of baseball … He’s one of the leaders on our ballclub, the longest-tenured Dodger currently. So I just have nothing but praise.”
“The ability to kind of adapt, start, come off the bench and still [do] whatever it takes to help the team win — he’s all-in. He does everything you want as a manager, everything.”
When reflecting on almost being out of the game and facing an early forced retirement in 2016, Muncy broke down.
“Man, there’s a lot with that,” Muncy said. “It’s just a lot.”
Now, nine seasons later, the 36-year-old slugger is a three-time All-Star, Dodger Stadium home run leader, Dodgers playoff home run leader and three-time World Series champion. But “Mad Max” focuses on his team’s success, not personal accolades.
“There’s not much when it comes to me, personally, that I care about,” Muncy said. “But three rings is definitely what I [cherish] most.”
Although Muncy may not focus on his personal statistics, his teammates take notice, not just of the player he is, but the man under the uniform.
“To know that he’s now the Dodger [Stadium] all-time home run leader? Whatever it is … after being an older guy in Triple-A with me and then getting called up … special,” Dodgers reliever Brock Stewart said of Muncy.
“I don’t know if he always believed in himself, and I can relate to that, because I didn’t believe in myself all the time … But to see him and how he persevered through that feeling [or] that self-doubt and became what he is now [is] super special.”
Muncy’s clutch playoff performance has given the Dodgers a chance to win another ring and “Hunt History” by becoming the first National League team to win three consecutive World Series. That role matters even more with Shohei Ohtani slumping. The Dodgers superstar went just 2-for-13 at the plate in the Dodgers NLDS matchup against the Braves. If the Dodgers are going to have any success in the NLCS, especially with the highest-paid and unanimously best baseball player on the planet playing like he’s in pee-wee back in Oshu, Japan, they will need their unsung hero, and Muncy’s teammates know they can rely on him.
“He’s a guy that is always going to show up for the team and do whatever it takes to put the team in a good position,” says Dodger infielder Miguel Rojas.
“He’s a guy you always can root for, especially in this organization full of stars. He always gets [overlooked] a little bit, but I feel like he’s one of the leaders of this club, and he will be until he retires.”
The Dodgers now turn their attention to the MLB’s winningest team this season, the Milwaukee Brewers, and the NLCS. Last year, the Dodgers swept the Brewers en route to their second straight World Series title. This time around, however, the Brewers are confident it will be a different story.
“We’re now as rested as they are,” Brewers owner Mark Attanasio said. “Because last year, we had a very emotional win against the Cubs and a lot of celebrating afterward, and the next day we’re in batting practice. And now we have the same number of days off as they do, and have (Jacob) Misiorowski and (Logan) Henderson and all our pitchers rested.
“So it’s our best against their best, and that’s always fun.”
On the Dodgers side, Manager Dave Roberts gave his club a simple yet clear message after their Game 4, series-clinching win in Atlanta.
“Eight more wins. Stay focused. Everybody in this room helped get us to where we are and where we’re gonna go,” Roberts said to his team in the locker room.
“In the postseason, guys, you don’t know when the moment is gonna come to you. All of us gotta stay focused and get ready.”
If Max Muncy has proven anything during his Dodgers tenure, it’s that he’s ready to do whatever it takes for this team to win and make history. Game 1 of the NLCS is set for Monday in Milwaukee.

item.dc:creator: Matt Levy

item.content:encoded:
Ladies and gentlemen, we’ve got ourselves a rematch.
Just like last year, Shohei Ohtani’s Los Angeles Dodgers and Christian Yelich’s Milwaukee Brewers are meeting in the NLCS.
And, once again, Pat Murphy’s club has home-field advantage. Games 1, 2, 6 and 7 will be at American Family Field in Milwaukee, WI.
Not everything about this Series is the same, though.
“I think it is different this year. … We’re going in to beat them,” Murphy told Fox Sports, referring to his team getting swept in 2025. “We earned it in the regular season to get home-field advantage. We’re going in to beat them, we don’t care who they have.”
If you’d like to be there to see if the Brew Crew really have what it takes to dethrone the defending World Series champion Dodgers, tickets are available for all four hypothetical contests in the Cream City.
At the time of publication, the lowest price we could find on seats for any one game in Milwaukee was $224 including fees on Vivid Seats.
Prices start at $144 including fees for fans hoping to attend a showdown at Dodger Stadium.
Ahead of the NLCS, Milwaukee battled with San Diego in a tense, back-and-forth four-game NLDS that saw instantly iconic moments like a clutch Jackson Chourio catch in Game 1, a Jackson Chourio walk-off single in Game 2 and Garrett Mitchell robbing Manny Machado of a home run in Game 4.
As for the Dodgers, the club continued their winning ways in the postseason [Editor’s Note: They haven’t lost a playoff series since the Diamondbacks beat them in the 2023 NLDS] and beat up on the formidable Braves.
Kiké Hernández smashed a home run — the 17th postseason dinger of his career, putting him ahead of Babe Ruth (!) on the all-time list — in the decisive fourth game and stellar offensive performances from Andy Pages and Max Muncy.
We can’t wait to see what comes next.
For more information, our team has everything you need to know and more about the Dodgers vs. Brewers 2026 NLCS below.
What do the cheapest tickets cost for NLCS games in Milwaukee?
A complete breakdown of all the best prices on tickets for every hypothetical game at Milwaukee’s American Family Field can be found here:

| Game 1 Sunday, Oct. 11 | $236 (including fees) |
| Game 2 Monday, Oct. 12 | $224 (including fees) |
| Game 6 Sunday, Oct. 18 | $235 (including fees) |
| Game 7 Monday, Oct. 19 | $277 (including fees) |
How much are the cheapest tickets for NLCS games in Los Angeles?
All of the cheapest potential Dodgers NLCS home game ticket prices are listed below.

|---|---|

| Game 4 Thursday, Oct. 15 | $150 (including fees) |

How can I watch the Dodgers vs. Brewers 2026 NLCS?
For fans who prefer to watch on the tube, you can catch this nervy series on FOX and FS1.
Both providers listed above can be found on the one-stop shop known as DIRECTV.
Huge 2026-27 concerts
Fans hoping to get a concert or three in this year too are in luck.
After a bit of digging, we found that many of the biggest names in music will be on the road this year and next.
Here are just five of the biggest acts and artists we can’t wait to see live in the near future.
• RUSH
Who else is out and about? Take a look at this list of all the biggest rockers on tour in 2026 to find the show for you.
This article was written by Matt Levy, New York Post live events reporter. Levy stays up-to-date on all the latest tour announcements from your favorite musical artists and comedians, as well as Broadway openings, sporting events and more live shows – and finds great ticket prices online. Since he started his tenure at the Post in 2022, Levy has reviewed a Bruce Springsteen concert and interviewed Melissa Villaseñor of SNL fame, to name a few. item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Dodgers will have time to reset rotation, bullpen, and struggling Shohei Ohtani for NLCS
item.dc:creator: Associated Press
item.description: ATLANTA — Finishing off the Atlanta Braves in four games in the NL Division Series meant more to the Los Angeles Dodgers than avoiding a winner-take-all Game 5. item.content:encoded:
ATLANTA — Finishing off the Atlanta Braves in four games in the NL Division Series meant more to the Los Angeles Dodgers than avoiding a winner-take-all Game 5.
By ending the series with a 4-1 victory, the Dodgers will have extra time to reset their rotation, bullpen and struggling slugger Shohei Ohtani for the Championship Series opening game.
"It's important. It was very important," Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. "Once you get to an elimination game, a Game 5 or a Game 7, anything can happen. And to be able to win today, get back, reset, have a day off tomorrow, set the rotation, it's huge."
The extra rest means Tarik Skubal likely will be the choice to start against Milwaukee instead of handling a Game 5 against the Braves. Similarly, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow will be well rested for their expected NLCS starts.
Infielder Miguel Rojas may need the extra rest for a sore lower back that kept him out.
Also, Edwin Díaz will have ample time to reset after recording saves on back-to-back days to close out the series against Atlanta. The ninth-inning work showed Díaz is re-established as the closer.
"The team trusts me," Díaz said. "I think that was the most important thing for me, the team trusts me. They give me the ball every single day. And the last two nights it's been amazing. That's why I came here to win games and close games like this one. So I'm really happy right now."
Despite those advantages, Roberts is preparing for a tough NLCS as the Dodgers try to move closer to their goal of becoming the first NL team to win three consecutive World Series.
"We've got our work cut out," Roberts said, adding extra rest also will be important for such players as Ohtani and Freddie Freeman.
Ohtani was 2 for 13 against Atlanta and hasn't homered since Aug. 18 while dealing with injuries to his right biceps, left knee and neck that have also kept the two-way player off the mound.
"So kind of enjoy this one, get Shohei a couple of days to get back," Roberts said. "Freddie, he had a big series, but, again a couple of days will help him. Give our guys in the 'pen a little reset. So we'll be ready to go Game 1."
Díaz pitched a perfect ninth inning in the clinching win. The on-field celebration was a low-key affair, but Roberts and his players, wearing "Take October" T-shirts and goggles to protect their eyes, soon were drenched with champagne.
The Dodgers made the most of their opportunity to celebrate another postseason series win while maintaining their focus on a third straight World Series championship.
"Our goal is to win the World Series, not this series," Díaz said. "We've got eight more wins to go. So our goal is win those eight games. And at the end of the day when we win those eight games, we celebrate.
"Now we're going back to LA to keep working. I know all the guys are on the same track. Now we just celebrate a little bit, go back to LA, get working and be ready for Sunday."
Andy Pages' bases-loaded single in the seventh drove in two runs to give the Dodgers a 3-1 lead. Max Muncy added to the lead with a homer in the ninth, his third blast of the postseason.
"Obviously, we have big teams, big series coming up," Pages said. "We're going to face tough teams, so prepare for those moments, but also take advantage of the opportunity of being here and enjoying these moments. And knowing that our ultimate goal is to win the World Series. So focus on that."

item.title: [Los Angeles Times] Commentary: He finally did it! Dodgers' Andy Pages ends two-year postseason slump at the perfect time

item.content:encoded:
- Click here to listen to this article
He pounded his chest twice as he left the batter’s box, and all of Dodgers nation rocked to the beat.
Andy Pages did it. He finally did it. He finally broke out of his baffling two-year October slump with a hit so powerful, he didn’t even have to climb over Kiké Hernández to get it.
How powerful? With one smooth swing he broke a tie by scoring two runs while sending two teams packing, the Atlanta Braves trudging home for the winter and the Dodgers charging into the National League Championship Series.
Yeah, it was a blast, both figuratively and literally, Pages’ two-out, two-strike bases-loaded single in the seventh inning Wednesday night silencing the lame tomahawk-chopping fans at Truist Park and giving the Dodgers an eventual clinching 4-1 victory against the Braves in the National League Division Series.
Certainly, it only gets tougher from here. In winning this best-of-five series three games to one, the Dodgers can now prepare for a best-of-seven showdown task against either the mighty Milwaukee Brewers or blazing San Diego Padres.
Yes, they will need to hit better, they will need Blake Snell to find his focus, they will need Shohei Ohtani to show up.
But…Andy Pages! Seriously! If a guy who was seven for 66 in the last two postseasons and was so helpless last year he was benched for the last three games of the World Series…if that guy can drive in the winning run from the bottom of the order? The once-fallible Dodgers may just be unbeatable.
“There’s no more talented team than the Los Angeles Dodgers,” manager Dave Roberts shouted in the postgame clubhouse. “We’re the best organization in sports, top to bottom. We’re smarter, we’re better, and we’re tougher.”
At that point, someone referenced a recent comment from Padres owner José E. Feliciano insinuating that the Dodgers, baseball’s oldest team, was composed of dinosaurs.
“And we’re dinosaurs!” shouted a voice above the clubhouse din.
If they’re dinosaurs, their first initial is “T” and their last name is ‘Rex.”
It’s OK to start seriously thinking about a three-peat now. They’re now just eight wins away but, given how mediocre the American League playoff teams appear, they could realistically be just four wins away.
Andy Pages comes through in the seventh inning to break a tie and four relievers close out a 3-1 victory over the Atlanta Braves to win the NLDS in four games.
Here’s guessing that the NLCS will be the real World Series. And here’s guessing the Dodgers will be ready.
Pages, who won the hearts of Dodger fans last October when he made a leaping game-saving catch over the back of Kiké Hernández, was granted his first big October swing thanks to the Braves largess.
In the seventh inning of a 1-all tie, Teoscar Hernández redeemed himself for another fielding blunder with a single that finally drove dizzying Tyler Mahle from the game.
In came Game 2 rookie sensation Didier Fuentes, only this time, he was all rookie and zero sensation, walking Josue De Paula and Kyle Tucker to load the bases. Considering De Paula is just a kid and Tucker has been struggling, the fact that both showed such patience in such a pressure situation was pretty cool. And moments later, it got even cooler.
In came veteran reliever Robert Suarez, and Pages was ready for him, working the count full before lining the two-run single up the middle.
The Dodgers added a run two innings later on a Max Muncy home run — has there ever been a playoff game when he hasn’t homered? — to finalize the score.
When the game ended on an Austin Riley fly out to right field, Pages celebrated in center field by taking off his cap, turning his face to the sky and pounding the cap three times into his glove.
It was a series that was worth the emotion, the Dodgers famous starting rotation giving up just four runs in 21 ⅓ innings, the bullpen solid behind a revived Edwin Díaz, and the offense doing just enough to beat Braves aces Chris Sale and Mahle.
In the fifth inning of a tie game, starter Tyler Glasnow issued walks to Riley and Michael Harris II. With two out, in came Alex Vesia. Up stepped slugger Matt Olson. The fans climbed to their feet. This was the Braves’ big chance.
But Olson swung at the first pitch and lined it directly to second baseman Kiké Hernández to end the threat and quiet the joint. Díaz threw a hitless ninth for his second save of the series and…who’s going to beat them?
Afterward, Roberts referenced nearly half of his team when talking about his pride. He talked about Pages’ hit, about De Paula’s walk, about reliever Edgardo Henriquez’s 1 ⅔ shutout innings, about Muncy’s bat and Freddie Freeman’s glove
“I guess, amazement,” he said. “Our guys just continue to fight, persevere. You never know who the guy’s going to be.”
The only glaring weakness was, once again, the superstar who used to be their strength. Ohtani scored the Dodgers’ first run after drawing a walk but went hitless in three ensuing at-bats. He only got two hits in the four-game series and you have to wonder if his injury-wracked body would be better out of the lineup.
How well are they playing without the full services of their most historic player? On the verge of making history, the Dodgers don’t even miss him.

item.content:encoded:
8 de octubre de 2026 - 9:55 PM
Atlanta - Andy Pages impulsó dos carreras con un sencillo con las bases llenas en la séptima entrada para darle la ventaja definitiva a Los Ángeles, y los reinante bicampeones Dodgers vencieron el miércoles 4-1 a los Braves de Atlanta para sentenciar su serie divisional de la Liga Nacional.
Los Dodgers ganaron juegos consecutivos en Atlanta para llevarse 3-1 la serie al mejor de cinco y avanzar a la Serie de Campeonato de la Liga Nacional dentro de empeño por convertirse en el primer equipo de la Liga Nacional que conquista tres Series Mundiales seguidas.
El cubano Pages conectó una línea por el centro a un lanzamiento en cuenta de 3-2 del venezolano Robert Suárez para remolcar al dominicano Teoscar Hernández, quien había empalmado un sencillo ante el abridor Tyler Mahle, y al corredor emergente Tommy Edman, para poner el 3-1 en el marcador 3-1.
Acto seguido, el colombiano Didier Fuentes concedió base por bolas al bateador emergente dominicano Josue De Paula y a Kyle Tucker para congestionar las bases. Edman corrió por De Paula.
El jonrón solitario de Max Muncy ante el cubano Raisel Iglesias en la novena aumentó la ventaja y dejó al toletero con un gran total de 19 cuadrangulares de postemporada con los Dodgers, ampliando su récord de la franquicia.
El derecho de los Dodgers Tyler Glasnow, en su primera apertura desde el 24 de septiembre, permitió apenas un hit, pero otorgó cinco bases por bolas en cuatro innings y dos tercios.
Después de conceder dos boletos en la quinta, el zurdo Alex Vesia terminó la entrada con un rodado de Matt Olson a la segunda base.
La oportunidad desperdiciada dejó a los Braves con 18 pasaporte en la serie, pero ninguno se concretó en carrera.
Glasnow y cuatro relevistas se combinaron para permitir apenas tres hits. Tanner Scott lanzó una octava entrada perfecta antes de que el puertorriqueño Edwin “Sugar” Díaz sacara tres outs rápidos para apuntarse el salvamento.
Fue el segundo salvamento en noches consecutivas para Díaz, de vuelta en el puesto de cerrador de los Dodgers.
Mahle, originario de Newport Beach, California, y que creció como aficionado de los Dodgers, permitió dos carreras —una limpia— en seis innings y un tercio.
Michael Harris II conectó el primer lanzamiento de Glasnow para un sencillo antes de robarse la segunda y, finalmente, anotar desde tercera con un lanzamiento descontrolado que rebotó en el protector de pecho del receptor Will Smith.
Los Dodgers empataron en la segunda con ayuda de dos errores de Atlanta. Shohei Ohtani recibió base por bolas, se robó la segunda y avanzó a tercera por un tiro desviado del receptor Sean Murphy hacia el jardín central. El elevado de Muncy a la zona corta del jardín izquierdo fue dejado caer por el campocorto hondureño Mauricio Dubón para otro error, lo que permitió que Ohtani anotara.
Hernández se estrelló contra la pared al intentar atrapar el doble de Ozzie Albies ante Vesia para abrir la sexta. Hernández se señaló la cabeza y el cuello al hablar con un preparador físico, pero se mantuvo en el juego.
El venezolano Edgardo Henríquez dejó varado a Albies en segunda. Henríquez permitió un hit al cubrir una entrada y dos tercios sin carrera para llevarse la victoria.
Las noticias explicadas de forma sencilla y directa para entender lo más importante del día.

item.title: [New York Post] Doctober classic propels Dodgers to NLCS in quest for World Series three-peat
item.dc:creator: Dylan Hernandez
item.description: ATLANTA — Dave Roberts didn’t hesitate. So what if Tyler Glasnow had thrown only 78 pitches? So what if he was still in the fifth inning? Glasnow had walked his second batter of the inning, and Roberts wasn’t about to take any chances. item.content:encoded:
ATLANTA — Dave Roberts didn’t hesitate.
So what if Tyler Glasnow had thrown only 78 pitches?
So what if he was still in the fifth inning?
Glasnow had walked his second batter of the inning, and Roberts wasn’t about to take any chances.
Calling on Alex Vesia to record the final out of the inning, Roberts initiated a chaotic sequence of events that resulted in the Dodgers claiming a 4-1 victory over the Braves in Game 4 of their National League Division Series.
The Dodgers advanced to the NL Championship Series.
Because of Tarik Skubal.
Because of Yoshinobu Yamamoto.
Because of Freddie Freeman.
And because of David Ray Roberts, the manager affectionately known as Doc who has a game or two like this every October.
The victory over the Braves on Wednesday was a Doctober classic.
On a day in which one of his four aces lasted only 4 ⅔ innings, Roberts figured out how to cover 13 outs of the game with a notoriously unpredictable bullpen.
Roberts’ fingerprints were also all over Andy Pages’ two-run single in the seventh inning that broke open the game.
When Teoscar Hernandez singled that inning with one out, Braves manager Walt Weiss replaced starting pitcher Tyler Mahle with right-hander Didier Fuentes.
Fuentes forced Max Muncy to ground out, but Hernandez advanced to second base on the play.
Due up was Game 3 hero Kike Hernandez.
Rather than have the right-handed utilityman face Fuentes, Roberts deployed rookie Josue De Paula as a pinch hitter. The left-handed-hitting De Paula drew a walk, at which point he was replaced on the basepaths by Tommy Edman.
Kyle Tucker followed up with another walk to load the bases, at which point Weiss turned to fireballer Robert Suarez to pitch to Pages.
Pages batted .078 in the postseason last year, which resulted in his benching in the World Series. He was 0-for-7 in the first two games of this series, but Roberts stuck with him.
Roberts’ faith was rewarded by the most important hit of Pages’ three-year career, a single to right field that drove in two runs to push the Dodgers in front, 3-1. The runs were the Dodgers’ first of the series that weren’t scored via a home run.
The manager demonstrated an equal level of creativity in directing his bullpen.
Vesia returned for the sixth inning, only to give up a leadoff double to Ozzie Albies. Roberts kept the left-hander in for another batter, the left-handed-hitting Drake Baldwin, who lined out.
Roberts’ next call to the bullpen was for Edgardo Henriquez, who spent the last two weeks of the regular season on the injured list. Henriquez gave up a run in the Dodgers’ Game 2 loss, but not only did Roberts trust him to prevent Albies from scoring, he also had him pitch the seventh inning.
From there, it was simple.
Tanner Scott pitched the eighth inning. With Muncy homering in the ninth inning to increase the lead to 4-1, Edwin Diaz came in to record the last three outs.
The Dodgers moved to within four wins of playing in their third consecutive World Series, and they did it with Shohei Ohtani still missing in action.
Ohtani was 2-for-13 in this series.
“It’s good to know that we can still win games without him doing a whole bunch,” Roberts said. “But he’s going to come to life. It will happen.”
Roberts has squinted extra hard in recent days to find evidence of that.
Here’s the reality: In his last 22 combined games between the regular season and playoffs, Ohtani has no home runs and only one RBI.
That isn’t a slump.
The No. 1 player in the game doesn’t go this long without hitting in the prime of his career without something being seriously wrong with him.
Ohtani spent 15 days last month on the injured list because of a discomfort in his right arm. A couple of days before he was placed on the IL, he said his left knee was also bothering him.
The uncertainty over Ohtani’s capabilities forced Roberts to move him around the lineup.
With Mookie Betts grinding out quality at-bats as the leadoff hitter and Freeman producing enough to solidify his place as the team’s No. 2 hitter, Ohtani was removed from the top of the order.
Against the left-handed Chris Sale in Game 3, Ohtani batted fifth. Against the right-handed Mahle on Wednesday, he batted cleanup.
Ohtani managed to create something out of nothing in the second inning. He drew a walk, then stole second base, prompting Braves catcher Sean Murphy to airmail a throw into center field. Ohtani scampered to third base. When Braves shortstop Mauricio Dubón dropped a popup by Muncy in shallow left field, Ohtani scored to tie the game at 1.
Ohtani didn’t collect any hits Wednesday, but he didn’t have to.
Roberts had the game under control.

item.title: [Field Level Media] Andy Pages' clutch hit sends Dodgers past Braves, into NLCS

The Dodgers, who won the series 3-1 and are looking to be the first National League team to win three straight World Series, await the winner of the other NLDS between the Brewers and Padres. item.content:encoded:
ATLANTA — Andy Pages’ two-run single in the seventh inning broke open a pitchers’ duel and helped the Los Angeles Dodgers close out their National League Division Series against the Atlanta Braves with a 4-1 win in Game 4 on Wednesday.
The Dodgers, who won the series 3-1 and are looking to be the first National League team to win three straight World Series, await the winner of the other NLDS between the Brewers and Padres. Milwaukee leads that best-of-five set 2-1 entering a Wednesday matchup in San Diego.
Pages’ hit was Los Angeles’ first with runners in scoring position in the series after the team started 0-for-14. It came off of Robert Suarez after Teoscar Hernandez hit a one-out single against Braves starter Tyler Mahle and then reliever Didier Fuentes issued back-to-back two-out walks.
Pages had two of the Dodgers’ five hits and two of their three RBIs in the win.
His clutch hit came the inning after Atlanta got nothing out of Ozzie Albies’ leadoff double, with Edgardo Henriquez (1-0) escaping the jam to earn his first career postseason victory.
Los Angeles’ Max Muncy tacked on an insurance run with a solo homer in the ninth, his third long ball of the postseason.
Mahle (0-1) was a tough-luck loser, charged with two runs (one earned) on three hits over 6 1/3 innings. He struck out four and walked one.
Michael Harris II had two of Atlanta’s three hits, including a double. However, the Braves’ situational hitting issues continued as they finished the series 1-for-23 with runners in scoring position.
Dodgers right-hander Tyler Glasnow battled through 4 1/3 innings, allowing just one run on one hit, walking five and striking out five. Alex Vesia, Henriquez, Tanner Scott and Edwin Diaz followed and combined to allow no runs on two hits over the final 4 1/3 innings, setting down the final seven Atlanta batters in a row.
Diaz earned his second save of the series.
Los Angeles’ pitching staff gave up eight runs on 18 hits over the four-game series.
The Braves opened the scoring in the bottom of the first on a wild pitch that scored Harris. He led off with a single, stole second and moved to third on a fielder’s choice.
The Dodgers equalized in the second behind a pair of Braves errors. Shohei Ohtani drew a leadoff walk, stole second and moved to third on an errant throw from catcher Sean Murphy. Muncy then hit a sky-high popup to shallow left that shortstop Mauricio Dubon dropped, allowing Ohtani to score.
–Curt Weiler, Field Level Media

item.title: [Orange County Register] Andy Pages comes through in the clutch to send Dodgers to NLCS
item.dc:creator: Bill Plunkett
item.description: ATLANTA — Overmatched last postseason and benched during the World Series, Andy Pages used the embarrassment to fuel an All-Star season in 2026. But he was hit by a pitch on Aug. 21 that broke a bone in his hand, didn’t return until the final six games of the regular season and started the postseason, trying to do too much (by his manager’s estimation) to make up for last fall’s lack of contributions. item.content:encoded:
ATLANTA — Overmatched last postseason and benched during the World Series, Andy Pages used the embarrassment to fuel an All-Star season in 2026.
But he was hit by a pitch on Aug. 21 that broke a bone in his hand, didn’t return until the final six games of the regular season and started the postseason, trying to do too much (by his manager’s estimation) to make up for last fall’s lack of contributions.
The accounts have been reconciled. It was Pages’ clutch two-out, two-run single in the seventh inning that broke a tie and lifted the Dodgers to a 4-1 victory on Wednesday night in Game 4 of their National League Division Series with the Atlanta Braves.
The victory sends the Dodgers to the National League Championship Series against either the Milwaukee Brewers or San Diego Padres. The Dodgers have reached baseball’s Final Four for the fifth time in the past seven years, the eighth time in the past 11. Their quest for a ‘three-peat’ will continue Sunday either in Milwaukee or at home against the Padres.
This series was decided in the seventh inning.
With the score tied 1-1, Teoscar Hernandez – fresh off a collision with the left field wall that left him on the warning track dirt, rubbing the left side of his head – singled with one out off Braves starter Tyler Mahle. It was just the third hit off Mahle and it came on just his 85th pitch. But Braves manager Walt Weiss went to his bullpen, bringing in Game 2 hero Didier Fuentes to face Max Muncy.
Fuentes got Muncy to ground out, Hernandez moving to second, but he walked pinch-hitter Josue De Paula and Kyle Tucker to load the bases with two outs.
Weiss had a quick hook, pulling Fuentes and handing the ball to veteran Robert Suarez to face Pages. Pages got ahead in the count, 3-and-1, then swung and missed at a 99.1 mph fastball from Suarez. He got another fastball on the full count and didn’t miss, stroking it through the middle for the Dodgers’ first – and only hit – with a runner in scoring position in their 16 at-bats in those situations during the four games of this series.
Runs had been hard to come by in Atlanta. After Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Chris Sale squared off in Game 3, Mahle and Tyler Glasnow allowed just a dirty run each through the first six innings.
In the bottom of the first, Michael Harris II led off with a single off of Glasnow. He stole second, went to third on a ground out and score when Glasnow spiked a knuckle curve in the dirt well in front of home plate. It bounced off Will Smith’s chest protector back towards the mound and Glasnow couldn’t retrieve it in time to get Harris.
In the top of the second, Shohei Ohtani took a five-pitch walk, stole second and went to third when Braves catcher Sean Murphy threw the ball into center field. Ohtani scored when Braves shortstop Mauricio Dubon dropped Max Muncy’s pop-up in shallow left field.
Mahle struck out only four in his 6⅓ innings (three of them consecutively in the fourth inning) and got just seven swings-and-misses on 95 pitches. But he got a lot of soft contact – and when he didn’t, it usually found a Braves fielder’s glove. The Dodgers hit seven balls in the first six innings with exit velocities of 95 mph or higher (the StatCast standard for “hard-hit”). Only one of them was a base hit – Pages’ third-inning single (106.7 mph).
Against Glasnow, the Braves just didn’t make much contact at all.
He gave up that leadoff single to Harris in the first inning but no other hits. He did walk five, though, including two in the fifth inning that prompted Manager Dave Roberts to pull him from the game after 78 pitches.
Dodgers pitchers somehow walked 18 batters in the series but let none of them score. Alex Vesia retired Matt Olson to end that fifth inning. Edgardo Henriquez held the Braves scoreless over the next two. Tanner Scott retired the slumping heart of the Braves’ order and Muncy gave Edwin Diaz cushion in the ninth inning with a solo home run (his 19th career postseason homer, a franchise record).
More to come on this story.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Andy Pages single beats Braves, Dodgers win NLDS in 4 games
item.dc:creator: Eric Stephen
item.description: It took until the seventh inning of the fourth game of the National League Division Series for the Dodgers to get their first hit with a runner in scoring position. But Andy Pages made it count, with a two-run single to break a tie in a 4-1 win over the Atlanta Braves on Wednesday night at Truist Park, clinching the NLCS to send the Dodgers to their third National League Championship Series in a row. The winning rally started with a single by Teoscar Hernández, just minutes after crashing into t
item.content:encoded:
It took until the seventh inning of the fourth game of the National League Division Series for the Dodgers to get their first hit with a runner in scoring position. But Andy Pages made it count, with a two-run single to break a tie in a 4-1 win over the Atlanta Braves on Wednesday night at Truist Park, clinching the NLCS to send the Dodgers to their third National League Championship Series in a row.
The winning rally started with a single by Teoscar Hernández, just minutes after crashing into the left field wall on a Braves double in the previous half-inning. That ended the night for Tyler Mahle, who continued to have the Dodgers number, once again pitching into the seventh.
In came Game 2 Braves hero Didier Fuentes, whose second batter faced was fellow 21-year-old pinch-hitter Josue De Paula, only 24 days his senior. De Paula, in just his second postseason plate appearance, walked, then was removed for pinch-runner Tommy Edman. Kyle Tucker also walked to load the bases, setting up Pages — the Dodgers RBI leader this season — to single home a pair.
After going hitless in his first two games this series, Pages had two hits in Game 3 and two more in Game 4, equaling his total for the entire postseason in 2025. The hit also snapped an 0-for-14 skid by the Dodgers with runners in scoring position to start this series.
The first of those runs snapped a string of 22 straight innings by Mahle against the Dodgers without allowing an earned run, dating all the way back to 2022.
Edgardo Henriquez, who entered with one out in the sixth inning and stranded a runner on second, followed with a scoreless seventh inning to bookend the Dodgers rally, and earned the win.
Just like in Game 3, Tanner Scott pitched a scoreless eighth and Edwin Díaz closed out the win in the ninth, giving the Dodgers the planned back end of their bullpen that hadn't really been fully intact since early April.
Dodgers pitchers allowed eight total runs in the four-game series.
Max power
Max Muncy added some insurance with a solo home run in the ninth inning, extending his Dodgers career postseason record with now 19 home runs. Muncy also homered in Games 1 and 2 of this series, matching his most prolific postseason series with the long ball. He also hit three home runs in the 2019 NLDS against the Washington Nationals.
Sloppy start
Both teams exchanged mistakes for each other's first run, including an errant throw into center field on a stolen base attempt from each side. Michael Harris II got a great jump from third base on a wild pitch by Tyler Glasnow that didn't get too far from home plate in the first inning, catching the Dodgers flat-footed. In the top of the second, Shohei Ohtani walked, stole second and went to third on the bad throw, then scored when a Max Muncy popup into short left field was biffed by shortstop Mauricio Dubón.
Glasnow improved a bit as the game progressed, and didn't allow another hit after Harris led off the game with a single. But, like Blake Snell in Game 2, Glasnow on Wednesday walked five batters, including two in the fifth inning — a leadoff free pass to Austin Riley after getting ahead 0-2, and a two-out, four-pitch walk to Ronald Acuña Jr. to end Glasnow's night early.
The Dodgers right-hander struck out five with those five walks in his 4 2/3 innings, and like Snell limited the damage to only one run. Alex Vesia helped, inducing a groundout to second base to end the fifth inning with those two Glasnow walks left stranded on base, and the game still tied.
Glasnow threw 78 pitches, 44 for strikes.
Not so free passes
None of Glasnow's five walks in Game 4 scored, and none of the 18 Braves who walked in the NLDS have touched home plate. But there have still been costs to that Dodgers wildness. For one, the Dodgers had to turn to its bullpen much earlier than hoped in two of the four games.
Also, two of Snell's walks in the first inning of Game 2, pushing Acuña to third base, which allowed him to score on an infield single. In Game 3, the pinch-hit walk by Rowdy Tellez pushed Dubón to third base, which allowed him to score on a groundout. So the walks have been costly, even if not as much as perhaps they should have been.
NLDS Game 4 particulars
Home run: Max Muncy (3)
WP — Edgardo Henriquez (1-0): 1 2/3 IP, 1 hit
LP — Tyler Mahle (0-1): 6 1/3 IP, 3 hits, 2 runs (1 earned), 1 walk, 4 strikeouts
Sv — Edwin Díaz (2): 1 IP, 1 strikeout
Up next
The Dodgers move on to a third consecutive National League Championship Series, and eighth in the last 11 years, beginning Sunday night (time TBD, Fox Sports) either in Milwaukee against the Brewers or at Dodger Stadium in Los Angeles against the Padres.

item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX -- A race to first based turned into a violent collision that sent two players sprawling onto the field and, eventually, into the dugout.
Arizona's Ildemaro Vargas and the Los Angeles Dodgers' Max Muncy are sore but otherwise OK, but, boy, what a jolt.
"It was terrible," Diamondbacks second baseman Ketel Marte said through an interpreter after hitting a walk-off homer in Arizona's 3-2 win over Los Angeles on Thursday night. "In my 10 years, I've never seen a collision like that."
It came in the fifth inning when Muncy hit a ground ball down the line over first base.
Vargas fielded the ball behind the bag, spun around and, seeing pitcher Ryne Nelson wasn't covering, took off running, hoping to beat Muncy.
He didn't and the full-speed collision sent both players flying in the air, landing with a thud on opposite sides of the base.
A hush fell over the crowd as both players writhed in the dirt and trainers from both teams rushed out. Vargas and Muncy were on the field for several minutes before slowly making their way to their respective dugouts.
"Those are the types of things that you see on the baseball field when two players are lying on the dirt after trying to make a hustle play," Diamondbacks manager Torey Lovullo said. "It's tough to see, but they both got off the field."
Muncy left with shortness of breath and was being evaluated for a concussion. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said he wouldn't play Friday against the Angels -- it was already a scheduled day off -- but could be available over the weekend.
Muncy told reporters he was a little banged up but will be all right.
"I really hope Vargas is OK -- I sent something over to him," he said. "I'm hoping he's doing all right and he's not too bad. But just bad situation that looks like neither of us knew which direction to go."
Vargas sustained bruises down his left side -- thigh, ribs and neck. X-rays were negative and he told Lovullo he would be ready to play Friday, if needed.
"My whole body feels like I ran into a truck, but thankfully all the exams and tests were negative," Vargas said through an interpreter.
It could have been much worse.br/]

item.content:encoded:
The Dodgers are back in Atlanta for Game 4 of the NLDS on Wednesday, needing just one more win to clinch the series. After getting to Chris Sale in Game 3, the Dodgers will face right-hander Tyler Mahle, who has turned heads since being acquired at the trade deadline from the San Francisco Giants.
After batting fifth in the starting lineup for the first time as a Dodger, Shohei Ohtani will once again be hitting in the middle third of the order, this time moving up to the cleanup spot with Teoscar Hernández sliding down to the fifth spot in the order.
Max Muncy makes his first start this series since batting 8th in Game 1 against left-hander Dylan Dodd, this time batting sixth in the lineup with Miguel Rojas getting the day off after dealing with back tightness. The hero of Game 3 on offense, Kiké Hernández, makes his second straight start, this time batting seventh while getting the start at second base. Kyle Tucker once again hits in the 8 spot while Andy Pages rounds things out after a multi-hit performance.
Runs have been hard to come by so far this series, as the Dodgers have plated just 10 combined runs over their first three postseason games, all of which have come via home runs. The main Achilles heel for the Dodgers has been their consistent inability to produce with runners in scoring position, as the team is 0-13 in those situations. The Braves, to their credit, have managed to get one hit with runners in scoring position, albeit across 14 at-bats, and have combined to score just eight runs over the first three games.
The Dodgers have fared well in previous matchups against Mahle, as the right-hander has a combined 3-3 record with a 3.15 ERA. Most of the damage came when Mahle was still with the Cincinnati Reds, and in his most recent start against the Dodgers back when he was with San Francisco, he shut them down over seven shutout innings in a 3-0 Giants win on April 22. Since joining Atlanta, Mahle finished the regular season with a 1.99 ERA and limited the Philadelphia Phillies to just one run in his most recent Wild Card start.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are coming off a massive Game 3 victory over the Atlanta Braves on the road at Truist Park on Tuesday night.
They’ll now take a 2-1 series lead into Wednesday’s matchup and sit just one win away from advancing to the NLCS as they continue to chase a third consecutive World Series title.
Ahead of the matchup. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts elected to make some changes to his starting lineup for the second straight day.
Dodgers Announce Teoscar Hernandez Change
Among those moving in the order is slugger Teoscar Hernandez, who hit third in the lineup Tuesday and will now drop to sixth for Game 4.
Hernandez is coming off back-to-back 0-for-4 performances. And Roberts will move catcher Will Smith into the No. 3 spot, while Shohei Ohtani moves from fifth to fourth and will bat cleanup.
Max Muncy will bat fifth in the lineup after starting Tuesday’s game on the bench.
Here’s the Dodgers starting lineup:

Looking at the Dodgers
L.A. has relied heavily on the long ball for its offense so far in this series against Atlanta.
After winning 5-3 in Game 1, losing 3-2 in Game 2 on Sunday and then winning 3-1 on Tuesday, all 10 of their combined runs in the series have come via home runs.
And they’ve seemingly done it with Shohei Ohtani being pretty much a non-factor at the plate.

item.title: [MLB.com] Dodgers' HR barrage continues with October Kiké's return, Freddie avenging robbery
item.dc:creator: Courtney Hollmon
item.description: ATLANTA -- After three scoreless innings of tight pitching at Truist Park, the Dodgers broke NLDS Game 3 open with a pair of fourth-inning home runs against Braves ace Chris Sale. The two-homer frame marks only the second time in Chris Sale’s postseason career that he has allowed multiple home runs in a single start. It happened previously on April 1, 2023, when Sale was with the Red Sox. Kiké Hernández provided the initial spark, crushing a 406-foot two-run shot to left field to break the score
item.content:encoded:
ATLANTA -- After three scoreless innings of tight pitching at Truist Park, the Dodgers broke NLDS Game 3 open with a pair of fourth-inning home runs against Braves ace Chris Sale.
The two-homer frame marks only the second time in Chris Sale’s postseason career that he has allowed multiple home runs in a single start. It happened previously on April 1, 2023, when Sale was with the Red Sox.
Kiké Hernández provided the initial spark, crushing a 406-foot two-run shot to left field to break the scoreless tie and put Los Angeles on the board. Just two batters later, Freddie Freeman delivered a dose of sweet-swinging revenge. After having a potential home run robbed by left fielder Mauricio Dubón in the third inning, Freeman made sure there was no doubt on his next trip to the plate, launching a solo shot deep into right-center field to extend the lead to 3-0.
The pair of big flies extended a historic postseason trend for Los Angeles: All 10 of the Dodgers' runs scored so far this postseason have come via the home run, marking the longest streak to start a postseason in MLB history.
Both home runs also provided individual milestones in the October record books.
For Hernández, the blast marked his first home run of the 2026 postseason and the 17th of his career, continuing his reputation as a clutch playoff hitter -- "October Kiké," if you will. He went 1-for-4 with two strikeouts.
“Experience helps a lot," Hernández said postgame on FOX. "Coming through in big moments helps a lot. Understanding that you can do it in the bigger moments. This is what I grew up dreaming about, playing October baseball. ... I’ve been lucky enough to play for two organizations that have put me there, and given me opportunities, and I’ve made the best of them.”
Freeman’s solo shot was his second of the 2026 postseason and the 18th of his playoff career, tying him with seven others for 10th on the all-time postseason home run list, including teammate Max Muncy, who got there in Game 2 of the NLDS. Freeman went 1-for-4 with a walk and a strikeout.
"It’s an extremely hard at-bat for a lefty," Freeman said of facing Sale on FOX. "I always say, against him, you’ve got to be prepared to die. Really, that’s the mindset. If you pull off of him, you have no chance. He’s throwing behind you and if he hits you in the ear, you’ve got to be ok with it. That’s my mentality, and thankfully I was able to get a good swing on some balls tonight.”

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have had plenty of postseason heroes during their World Series runs in 2024 and 2025.
Last year, the biggest may have been backup infielder Miguel Rojas, who hit a game-tying home run in Game 7 against the Toronto Blue Jays in the ninth inning.
As a result, Rojas has continued to get opportunities in 2026 and was inserted into the starting lineup for Game 3 against the Atlanta Braves in this year's NLDS. He also started Game 2 in place of Max Muncy at third base.
Oct 6, 2026; Cumberland, Georgia, USA; ]Los Angeles Dodgers second baseman Miguel Rojas (72) throws to first base for an out against the Atlanta Braves during the first inning in game three of the NLDS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Truist Park. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)
Rojas was put in to hit against Braves left-hander Chris Sale given his platoon advantage as a right-handed hitter. It did not work out through his first three at-bats as he went 0-for-3 with a strikeout.
Rojas remained in the game for a fourth at-bat in the eighth inning against Braves reliever Brent Suter, who is also a southpaw.
Unfortunately, he did not finish the at-bat. After fouling off the second pitch he immediately reached for his lower back with his left arm.
A trainer came out to visit Rojas and after a brief discussion he was removed from the game with Tommy Edman taking over mid at-bat. Edman popped up shortly after. The Dodgers released an update shortly after. "Miguel Rojas left tonight's game with low back pain," the team wrote on X.
Latest Update on Miguel Rojas
During the broadcast, Ken Rosenthal of The Athletic reported that Rojas originally suffered the setback while fielding a ground ball back in the 5th inning.
If Rojas' injury is serious enough to keep him out for the remainder of the NLDS, the Dodgers would have to replace him on the roster.
That would also keep him out of the NLCS should Los Angeles advance, which would be a huge loss given the postseason experience he brings.

He was replaced by Tommy Edman, who popped out on the first pitch he saw. Rojas drew the start with the left-handed Chris Sale on the mound. It was his second consecutive start after he got the nod in Ga
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers infielder Miguel Rojas has exited Game 3 of the National League Division Series in the top of the eighth inning with an injury.
Rojas appeared to tweak his lower back on a swing and is now out of the game. He initially tweaked his back on a defensive play earlier in the game.
He was replaced by Tommy Edman, who popped out on the first pitch he saw.
Rojas drew the start with the left-handed Chris Sale on the mound. It was his second consecutive start after he got the nod in Game 2 with the lefty Ray Kerr starting.
After going 1-for-1 against Kerr before being replaced by Max Muncy, Rojas was 0-for-3 on Tuesday.
What is Miguel Rojas' Injury?
The Dodgers announced Rojas exited the game with low back pain.
Is Miguel Rojas Retiring After This Season?
Rojas is in the midst of what's expected to be his final season in Major League Baseball. The 37-year-old entered the year saying this would be his last. However, he then left the door open for a potential return in 2027 if the Dodgers won the World Series this year.
Before Tuesday's game, Rojas spoke to reporters and still didn't have a firm answer.
"I'm not thinking about that at all. I'm not thinking about my future or anything," Rojas said. "In regards to my retirement or stepping away from the game, I will never think about stepping away from the game because of my performance or my way to play my game. I think there's other things in life that I'm contemplating about that decision. But if I have to tell you right now, I'm not 100% like [Clayton] Kershaw was last year or others in the past that knew for sure they want to go after this year.
"For me it's more, I would say it's a 40/60 right now that I want to stay in the game and I want to play. But it's not about me. It's about the organization. It's about doing what we're supposed to do to help the team win this year. And then after that we will have conversations."
Rojas, who hit the game-tying home run in Game 7 of the 2025 World Series against the Toronto Blue Jays, had a strong season in 2026, appearing in 105 games and hitting .267 with and OPS of .703. He's still an elite defender in the infield.
Off the field, he's a leader in the Dodgers clubhouse.
Manager Dave Roberts will have an update on his veteran after the game.

item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts named potential players who could get a spot in the starting lineup for NLDS Game 3.
The Dodgers' offense hasn't been its best through the first two games of the series, relying exclusively on homers to score all seven of their runs so far. A change of personnel could help the Dodgers string together some hits and bring some more runs across.
Ahead of Tuesday's matchup, Roberts named three players who could insert themselves into the lineup for NLDS Game 3.
"You've got Kiké [Hernandez], you've got [Miguel Rojas], you've got Muncy," Roberts said.
Hernandez provides plenty of positional versatility for the Dodgers, and could stand in at a number of positions if the Dodgers want to approach their matchup against the left-handed Chris Sale with a lineup full of right-handed batters.
The fan favorite's most likely role if he were to start Game 3 would be as the third baseman, keeping left-handed third baseman Max Muncy out of the lineup for a second consecutive game despite hitting homers in each of the first two games of the series, but he could also play either of the corner outfield spots if needed.
Rojas would stand in at second base for Tommy Edman in the most likely case, as Roberts isn't quite ready to move Edman into center to replace Andy Pages despite his rough postseason record.
Who Won't Start for the Dodgers on Tuesday?
In addition to those three players, Roberts revealed Josue De Paula won't have a starting spot against Sale.
"Josue De Paula I don't see being an option," Roberts said.
As a left-handed batter, De Paula's omission from the lineup makes plenty of sense, and he will be available off of the bench for the remainder of the game.
Other than De Paula, Hyeseong Kim and Hunter Feduccia almost certainly won't start, but the rest of the lineup could change as the Dodgers look to find a spark in their offense. With the series tied at one game apiece, the Dodgers need to claim victory in one of their two games in Atlanta to ensure they return home for a game if necessary.
Game 3 could swing momentum in the Dodgers' direction, and they'll do anything to take the lead in the NLDS. Tuesday's game begins at 3:00 p.m. PT.

item.title: [DodgersBeat] Dave Roberts Ponders Dodger Lineup Tweaks Ahead of Game 3

item.content:encoded:
ATLANTA, GA — Dave Roberts spent Monday weighing changes on both sides of the ball before Game 3 in Atlanta.
The Dodgers manager said he is considering lineup tweaks against Chris Sale, including the possibility of moving Shohei Ohtani lower in the order. He also made it clear that Edwin Díaz has worked his way back into serious ninth-inning consideration after his sharp outing in Game 2.
With the NLDS tied 1-1, Roberts sounded open to adjusting quickly.
Díaz Could Close
“I think that we’ve built him up, regained the confidence in him and himself,” Roberts said of Díaz. “I think that it’s certainly a viable option for tomorrow night. I feel very confident with him finishing a game.”
Roberts said Díaz’s most recent outing was about as good as he has seen from him.
“That last outing was as good as we’ve seen him throw, and it’s hard to imagine throwing any better,” Roberts said. “He’s put himself in a position to be the closer.
“In October, I don’t pay too much attention to the long sample of a season in a lot of cases, because in October things happen quickly and you’ve got to be willing to read and react.”
Roberts also praised the way Díaz handled a difficult season.
“Character,” he said. “That’s the main thing. When things aren’t going the best and how players respond, that’s telling.
“The way he stayed the course, dealt with the injuries, went to OKC on a longer rehab to work things out and then took on whatever role we had for him says a lot about him.”
Lineup Changes Are on the Table
Roberts also acknowledged that the Dodgers could look different against Sale.
“I am considering it,” he said. “I think that’s a very fair question. I have to be mindful of it being two games, and then within those two games, what have I seen? Are we seeing good at-bats?”
He pointed to Will Smith as someone whose results have not matched the quality of his plate appearances.
“I think Will Smith is taking good at-bats, just missing some pitches, taking good swings, not chasing much,” Roberts said. “Versus other people maybe expanding, trying to do too much.
“Those are things that you’re trying to make bets on. Then you’re looking at tomorrow with Sale, the history, recency, how guys are prepared and will prepare for Sale. So yeah, I’m thinking through that, and there are possible changes.”
Roberts listed Kiké Hernández, Miguel Rojas and Max Muncy among the options he could work into the lineup.
“At the end of the day, our guys are our guys,” he said. “I can tweak a lineup. I can insert, take out a player or two, but we still have to go out there and play, execute and take good at-bats.”
Moving Ohtani Is Possible
Roberts said he would consider moving Ohtani further down in the order if he believes it helps the team.
“I would,” he said. “I think moving him from one to two, but going further than that, I’m open to it.
“If I do, I would obviously have the conversation with Shohei to explain why. At the end of the day, every conversation I’ve had with him is whatever is best for the team, he’s all in on. I know that undoubtedly.”
Roberts thinks some of Ohtani’s recent issues have come from trying to do too much.
“I think there’s a little bit of trying to do too much,” he said. “Everything orbits around Shohei in the sense of his talent, and the Braves are going to enter with caution. They’re going to continue to expand as long as we keep giving that to them.
“Until we show some discipline, they’re going to continue to use that playbook.”
He also said Ohtani may be pressing for power.
“Hitting homers, slugging is so much a part of his hallmark in the batter’s box,” Roberts said. “He’s very in tune with what’s being said, what he hasn’t done.
“But that base hit the other way yesterday, that’s production. Against a guy like Chris Sale, that gives you a chance. Trying to chase slug tomorrow night might not be the right plan given the starter.”
Roberts Still Believes in Pages
Andy Pages has also struggled, but Roberts said he plans to keep giving him chances.
“I’m going to continue to give Andy leash,” Roberts said. “I believe in him. I feel that for us to win the World Series this year, we’re going to need him to be an active part of our team.
“This is, for me, given how he has come into the postseason, too small of a sample. He has taken two walks. Tomorrow is not going to be the end-all, be-all because Sale is a tough matchup, but I still want to see good at-bats.”
Roberts believes the main issue is pressing.
“I think there’s trying to do too much,” he said. “When he came back, he was swinging the bat really well, had success, and now I think there’s a little bit of trying too much.”
Freeman Looks Healthier
One hitter Roberts feels especially good about is Freddie Freeman.
“I think he’s gotten into his legs a lot more,” Roberts said. “He’s moving balls in the hitting zone forward. He’s as healthy as he’s been in quite some time. I think the mechanics are sound.”
Roberts credited the five-day break with helping Freeman get his knee into better shape.
“The week off was really crucial for him,” he said. “Being able to manage that with the five days off got him back to health to be able to work through some things without having to perform in a game setting.”
Sale vs. Yamamoto
Roberts expects Sale to attack the Dodgers much the same way he did when Atlanta faced them in August.
“The fastball just sort of bullied us at the top of the zone,” Roberts said. “There was some chase down below, and with the lefties, throwing more two-seamers to keep us honest in and then expand away.”
Still, Roberts believes the Dodgers are in a better offensive place than they were then.
“I do think we are in a different spot,” he said. “The stakes are certainly higher. There is familiarity on both sides. I think we’ll see better at-bats.
“Chris is going to be tough regardless. We know that. We know we’re going to be in for a dogfight, but I just don’t see him bullying us like he did his last start.”
And Roberts feels good about the pitcher the Dodgers will send out against him.
“There should be a lot of talk about Chris Sale, but our guy’s pretty dang good,” Roberts said. “He’s been a very good pitcher in the postseason, so we feel very good about that.
“I think both pitchers are going to pitch well. It’s kind of who grinds out at-bats best.”
More Dodgers Coverage:
Have you subscribed to the Bleed Los Podcast YouTube channel? Be sure to ring the notification bell to watch player interviews, participate in shows & promotions, and stay up to date on all Dodgers news and rumors!
A lifelong baseball fan, Webb has been going to Dodger games since he moved to Los Angeles in 1987. His favorite memory was attending the insane Game 3 of the World Series in 2025 and hugging random Dodgers fans after Freddie’s walkoff homer. He has been writing for Dodgersbeat since 2020.

item.title: [Los Angeles Times] Move Shohei Ohtani down in the Dodgers' lineup? Dave Roberts is 'open' to it

item.content:encoded:
Move Shohei Ohtani down in the Dodgers’ lineup? Dave Roberts is ‘open’ to it
- Click here to listen to this article
ATLANTA — As the Dodgers mull potential lineup changes for Game 3 of the National League Division Series, manager Dave Roberts said he is “open” to moving Shohei Ohtani lower in the batting order.
In his three seasons with the Dodgers, Ohtani has batted first or second in every game he has started. However, as he has admitted he is trying to “manage” in the aftermath of knee and arm injuries, and as Roberts has acknowledged Ohtani is “not 100%,” the lack of success could compel the manager to replace him at the top of the lineup with a more productive hitter at some point.
“I would,” Roberts said Monday. “I would. I think it’s something that, you know, I think moving him from 1 to 2 — but going further than that? I’m open to it.
“And it’s something that if I do, I would obviously have the conversation with Shohei to explain why. And at the end of the day every conversation I’ve had with him is whatever’s best for the team, he’s all-in on. So I know that undoubtedly.”
It would be strange for the Dodgers to bench Shohei Ohtani, but it’s clear that pretending he’s healthy enough to provide meaningful at-bats isn’t helping.
The Dodgers are batting .215 through the first two games of the NLDS, with the Atlanta Braves scheduled to pitch left-handed ace Chris Sale in Game 3 on Tuesday. If the Dodgers lose, they would need to win back-to-back elimination games to advance beyond this series.
Roberts said the lineup changes he would consider include starting Kiké Hernández and Miguel Rojas, both of whom hit well against left-handers. That could mean infielders Max Muncy (0 for 7 against Sale, with five strikeouts) and Tommy Edman (0 for 11 against Sale) might not start.
Center fielder Andy Pages, who batted so poorly last October he was benched for the final three games of the World Series, is hitless in seven at-bats in this series, with four strikeouts.
“I’m gonna continue to give Andy leash,” Roberts said. “I believe in him. I feel that for us to win the World Series this year, we’re gonna need him to be an active part of our team.
Roberts said he did not envision benching catcher Will Smith, who is 0 for 8 in the series. The Dodgers’ backup catcher, Hunter Feduccia, is a career .205 hitter with no postseason experience.
But, even with the Dodgers’ star-studded lineup, the spotlight shines brightest on Ohtani.
Ohtani has not homered since Aug. 18. He hit .157 between then and the end of the regular season, striking out in 41% of his at-bats. In this series, he has two hits and two strikeouts in eight at-bats, and his inability to refrain from swinging at pitches outside the strike zone has become a glaring weakness.
“He’s not 100%,” Roberts said. “But, at the end of the day, he can still do a better job of staying in the strike zone.”
Ohtani hasn’t given the Braves a reason to challenge him within the strike zone.
“Everything orbits around Shohei, in the sense of his talent,” Roberts said. “And the Braves are going to enter with caution. And, so, knowing that, they’re going to continue to expand as long as we keep giving that to them. So until we show some discipline, they’re going to continue to kind of use that playbook.”

That’s what dynamic manager Dave Roberts was grappling with on Monday, as the Dodgers gathered at Truist Park in Atlanta ahead of Game 3 of their National League Division Series against the Braves. item.content:encoded:
ATLANTA –– The Dodgers don’t want to overreact to a two-game sample size.
But, with elimination all of a sudden just two games away, they don’t want to wait too long to make changes either.
That’s what dynamic manager Dave Roberts was grappling with on Monday, as the Dodgers gathered at Truist Park in Atlanta ahead of Game 3 of their National League Division Series against the Braves.
A daunting challenge awaits on Tuesday night, when the club will face Braves ace Chris Sale for the first time since he threw a complete-game shutout against them in August.
Thus, even though the team’s quest for a World Series three-peat just began, potential lineup changes were already under consideration.
And even superstar Shohei Ohtani might not be immune.
“I am considering [changes],” Roberts said. “I think that’s a very fair question.”
That didn’t mean Roberts was ready to commit to any significant alterations ahead of a pivotal Game 3, with the best-of-five series tied one game apiece.
He noted the danger of reading too far into small playoff sample sizes this early in the postseason.
Still, he said there were things he was “thinking through” and “possibly kind of some changes” that could be enacted on Tuesday.
One possibility: Inserting Miguel Rojas and/or Kiké Hernández into lineup, perhaps in place of Max Muncy and/or Tommy Edman, to give the Dodgers extra right-handed bats against a dominant left-hander in Sale.
Another, more notable potential option: Moving Ohtani even further down the order from his current No. 2 spot, after he went just 2-for-8 in the first two games of the NLDS while continuing to battle right arm and left knee injuries.
“[We already moved] him from 1 to 2 –– but going further than that? I’m open to it,” Roberts said. “It’s something that, if I do, I would obviously have the conversation with Shohei to explain why.”
The explanation, of course, wouldn’t be too complicated.
In Ohtani’s currently diminished physical state, he has simply not been the same presence at the top of the order that the Dodgers have grown accustomed to from the four-time MVP.
“Like we’ve talked about, he’s not 100%,” Roberts said.
But also, “I think there’s a little bit of [him also] trying to do too much,” Roberts added. “I think that’s a piece.”
Indeed, Ohtani has suffered from a futile combination so far in the playoffs, failing to either punish pitches over the plate or keep from chasing out of the strike zone.
“It’s hard to have success when you’re out of the zone,” Roberts said. “So I think that’s the thing, then the question is: How do we get him [attacking pitches back] into it?”
A change of mindset could help, especially against a premium pitcher like Sale (who has held Ohtani to a 3-for-15 mark with five strikeouts and only one double in their career head-to-head matchups).
“Trying to chase slug tomorrow night might not be the right plan, given the starter,” Roberts said.
Instead, Roberts pointed to the opposite-field single Ohtani slapped past a shift for his lone hit in Sunday’s Game 2 loss.
“That at-bat yesterday, the block base hit the other way, that’s something that is production,” Roberts said. “I think that’s something where, against a guy like Chris Sale, it gives you a chance.”
The Dodgers, of course, would love to get more pop from Ohtani, who led the team with eight home runs during last year’s World Series trek. Roberts also knows the slugger “feels the responsibility” to provide such power, which might be contributing to his lack of plate discipline.
Thus, for now, taking the pressure off Ohtani’s shoulders by potentially hitting him lower in the lineup might also prove to be prudent.
“At the end of the day, every conversation I’ve had with him is whatever’s best for the team,” Roberts said. “And he’s all in on [that]. I know that undoubtedly.”
While Roberts will contemplate other changes beyond Ohtani’s spot in the order, there were a few ideas he outright struck down Monday night.
The big one: Removing Andy Pages from the batting order despite his 0-for-7 start in the playoffs –– one that has felt reminiscent of his historic struggles last October, and been further marred by a consequential ABS challenge he missed in Game 1.
While Roberts said he feels Pages has been “trying to do too much” –– downplaying any lingering effects from the fractured hand that sidelined the center fielder for most of September –– he also said he wanted to give the 25-year-old slugger more leash.
“I believe in him,” Roberts said. “And I feel that for us to win the World Series this year, we’re gonna need him to be an active part of our team.”
That was all part of the balance Roberts was trying to strike with his team’s season potentially hanging in the balance. It might still feel early for drastic changes. But one more loss, and the club’s three-peat bid will be on the brink.
“Our guys are our guys,” Roberts said. “Yeah, I can tweak a lineup. I can kind of insert, take out a player or two. But at the end of the day, we still have got to go out there and play and execute and take good at-bats.”

item.content:encoded:
MILWAUKEE -- Los Angeles Dodgers utilitymanKiké Hernandezis expected to be activated in time to make his season debut Monday after recovering from surgery on his left elbow.
Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said Sunday that Hernández should be available for the start of their home series against the Colorado Rockies.
"There's a different energy with Kiké," Roberts said Sunday. "There's a levity. There's an intensity. There's a good worker in there, a winning player. So I'm looking forward to having that edge."
Hernández, 34, signed a one-year, $4.5 million contract in February that kept him with the Dodgers. He underwent surgery last fall that kept him from playing for Puerto Rico in the World Baseball Classic and delayed the start of his 2026 season.
He hit .214 with a .298 on-base percentage with three RBIs in 12 games while on a rehabilitation assignment with Oklahoma City. He batted .203 with a .255 on-base percentage, 10 homers and 35 RBIs in 92 games with Los Angeles last season.
Hernández often has done his best work in October while helping the Dodgers win World Series in 2020, 2024 and 2025. He has batted .272 with an .826 OPS, 16 homers and 42 RBIs in 103 postseason games.
His return comes while Dodgers third baseman Max Muncy recovers after a 95.5 mph sinker from Milwaukee's Aaron Ashby hit him in the right wrist on Friday. X-rays were negative and the Dodgers expressed optimism that Muncy avoided a major injury.
"We were resolved to not having him available this weekend," Roberts said. "My expectation is that he's getting a little bit better today and maybe swing a bat tomorrow to see. I don't expect him in the lineup tomorrow either."
Muncy is batting .258 with a .363 on-base percentage, .515 slugging percentage, 12 homers and 19 RBIs in 48 games.

item.content:encoded:
El colombiano Didier Fuentes lanzó tres entradas y dos tercios desde el bullpen de los Bravos de Atlanta, ponchó a Shohei Ohtani y ayudó a la victoria por 3-2 sobre los Dodgers de Los Ángeles en el Dodger Stadium. El resultado dejó igualada 1-1 la otra Serie Divisional de la Liga Nacional.
Fuentes ingresó en el sexto episodio y permitió un imparable y una carrera limpia, sin otorgar bases por bolas. Realizó 47 lanzamientos, de los cuales 30 fueron strikes, y logró tres ponches durante su primera actuación de postemporada.
El relevista colombiano enfrentó a Ohtani con cuenta completa. Luego de una recta a 162,4 km/h, que fue declarada bola, recurrió a una bola curva 137,3 km/h, para conseguir el tercer strike.
También retiró por la vía del ponche a Will Smith y Freddie Freeman. Fuentes dominó a los primeros 11 bateadores que enfrentó, hasta que Max Muncy conectó un cuadrangular con dos outs en el noveno inning.
Esa es la racha más larga de un relevista de 21 años o menos en un juego de postemporada en la historia de la MLB. Ningún relevista de 21 años o menos ha tenido una racha tan larga en un juego de temporada regular desde Tom Gordon el 12 de abril de 1989, según lo publicado por Opta Stats en su perfil de X.
El único punto negativo de la jornada para el joven beisbolista cafetero fue el jonrón de Muncy impulsó la entrada de Iglesias, quien retiró al único bateador al que se enfrentó para conseguir la victoria. Pero eso no arruinó lo que fue una noche memorable para Fuentes, quien lanzó cuatro rectas a más de 99 mph en la novena entrada.
“Fue muy emotivo y emocionante. Así que le doy gracias a Dios por la ayuda que me ha permitido mantenerme sano y poder competir”, dijo el nacido en Tolú, Sucre, tras su primera gran noche en la liga más importante de béisbol en el mundo.
“¿Tiene 21 o 22 años? Está haciendo eso a esa edad. Es increíble, sobre todo lanzar a 100 millas por hora. Se enfrenta a situaciones de alto nivel y las supera. Fue realmente impresionante” dijo Kerr, el lanzador principal de los Bravos de Atlanta, sobre Fuentes.
Mientras que Matt Olson, primera base de los Bravos, se refirió a la potencia en el brazo que tiene el colombiano: “No podía creer que volviera a lanzar en la novena entrada, pero lo hizo y seguía lanzando a 100 millas por hora. Eso fue impresionante.”
“Después de su tercera entrada, miré a nuestro entrenador de lanzadores y le dije: ‘Veamos cómo se siente’”, dijo Weiss. “Si se siente bien, quiero que vuelva a lanzar. No quería cambiar algo que funcionaba bien. Estaba lanzando muy bien”, declaró el manager del equipo.
Los Bravos habían abierto el marcador con un sencillo productor de Mauricio Dubón en el primer episodio. Freeman igualó para los Dodgers con un jonrón solitario en el cuarto, pero Atlanta volvió a tomar la ventaja en el quinto mediante una jugada que permitió anotar a Michael Harris II.
Harris amplió el marcador en el séptimo con un doblete productor que llevó a Matt Olson al plato. Fuentes se anotó su primer hold, la estadística asignada a un relevista que preserva una ventaja en una situación comprometida. La serie se trasladará a Atlanta para el tercer juego, programado para el martes a las 5:00 p. m., hora de Colombia.
En las Series Divisionales con el formato actual 2-2-1, los equipos que consiguen dividir victorias como visitantes antes de regresar a casa para los Juegos 3 y 4 han ganado la serie 30 de 49 veces (61%).

item.title: [heavy.com] Dodgers’ Mookie Betts Makes Feelings Clear After Loss to Braves
item.dc:creator: Keith Watkins
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers are heading to Atlanta with their home-field advantage gone. A 3-2 loss in Game 2 of the National League Division Series on Sunday night evened the series at one game apiece and handed the Braves exactly the split they were looking for. The Dodgers failed to deliver a single hit in eight chances with runners in scoring position over the two home games. The offense that was supposed to carry them through October has yet to find a consistent rhythm. After the loss, one of t
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are heading to Atlanta with their home-field advantage gone. A 3-2 loss in Game 2 of the National League Division Series on Sunday night evened the series at one game apiece and handed the Braves exactly the split they were looking for.
The Dodgers failed to deliver a single hit in eight chances with runners in scoring position over the two home games. The offense that was supposed to carry them through October has yet to find a consistent rhythm.
After the loss, one of the team’s veteran leaders offered a straightforward assessment of where things stand.
Betts Sets the Tone for Atlanta
Mookie Betts did not sugarcoat the challenge but refused to frame the situation as a crisis.
“It’s just not gonna be easy,” Betts said. “But I mean we knew that from the beginning… We know it’s gonna be a tough matchup, no matter who’s on the mound.”
The comment reflected the mentality of a player who has been through deep October runs before. Betts helped the Dodgers win titles in 2024 and 2025. He knows what the grind looks like, and he knows that a tied series heading into a road game is far from a death sentence.
Still, there was no dodging what happened Sunday. The Dodgers had their best opportunity in the fifth inning with two runners on and nobody out but came away empty. Six different Braves relievers held the lineup in check for the majority of the night.
Betts’ Game 2 Showed the Problem
Betts finished 0-for-2 with a pair of walks in Game 2. He reached base, drew pitches, and did his part to set the table from the leadoff spot. The production behind him did not follow.
The Dodgers collected just four hits beyond Freddie Freeman‘s game-tying home run in the fourth. Max Muncy added a solo shot in the ninth to pull within a run, but by then the damage had been done.
Through two games, the pattern is clear. When the lineup cannot string hits together, it relies on the long ball. That approach has a ceiling, and the Dodgers hit it Sunday.
LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA – OCTOBER 03: Mookie Betts #50 of the Los Angeles Dodgers throws to first base during the seventh inning against the Atlanta Braves in game one of the National League Division Series at Dodger Stadium on October 03, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images)
Final Word for the Dodgers
Chris Sale is waiting in Atlanta. The Braves ace held the Dodgers scoreless when the two teams met in the regular season and will have the benefit of additional rest heading into Game 3 on Tuesday.
Betts’ message was simple. This was never going to be easy. The series is tied, the road gets harder, and the Dodgers need their lineup to find a way beyond home runs.
Two games in, that is the one thing they have not figured out.
